This document is the stenographic report of the 76th session of the 21st legislative period of the German Bundestag, held on Wednesday, May 6, 2026. The session began with the expansion and handling of the agenda, and the subsequent removal of agenda item 6c. The primary focus of the session was the "Befragung der Bundesregierung" (Questioning of the Federal Government). Several ministers and Members of Parliament (MPs) participated in discussions, with Federal Minister Reem Alabali Radovan (BMZ) and Federal Minister Bärbel Bas (BMAS) being frequently mentioned. MPs from various parties, including AfD, BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN, CDU/CSU, SPD, and Die Linke, posed questions and made statements. While the content of the debates is not fully detailed in this index, the extensive list of speakers and the page numbers indicate a substantial discussion took place. facts.fact: In ancient Rome, the color purple was so expensive and difficult to produce (derived from a specific species of sea snail) that only emperors and high-ranking officials were permitted to wear it. This strict sumptuary law helped solidify purple as a symbol of imperial power and wealth, and even commoners wearing it could face severe punishment.

The tradition of bowing in many East Asian cultures, particularly in Japan, has deep roots in Confucian philosophy which emphasizes hierarchy, respect, and social harmony. The depth and duration of the bow convey the level of respect and the social standing of the individuals involved, making it a nuanced form of non-verbal communication.
